# Preface {.unnumbered}

This companion follows the slides of **Chapter 1: The Wave Nature of Light** (Basics of Optoelectronics, University of
Trento) section by section. The slides tell the story; this book lets you **compute it**. Every figure is made by a few
lines of Python that you can unfold ("Show the Python"), copy and modify. The **live panels** (marked with a blue bar on
the left) recompute directly in your browser. They need no installation.

[![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/{{< var github_user >}}/{{< var repo >}}/blob/main/{{< var subdir >}}/notebooks/interactive_explorers.ipynb) &nbsp;Interactive explorers in Google Colab (no installation, Google account needed).

## Where this chapter sits in the course

Chapter 1 gives the toolkit for everything that follows: waveguides and fibers (Ch. 2), LEDs and semiconductor optics
(Ch. 3), lasers and amplifiers (Ch. 4), photodetectors (Ch. 5), and polarisation and modulation (Ch. 6). The slide-9
example of a 5G network already contains most of this chapter. Light is a wave guided by total internal reflection,
filtered by interference, multiplexed by gratings, and reflected by Bragg mirrors.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sign convention (read this once)
The slides (following Kasap) use the **engineering convention** $E\propto\exp[j(\omega t-kz)]$, which gives a complex
index $N=n-jK$ and a relative permittivity $\varepsilon_r=\varepsilon_r'-j\varepsilon_r''$. Most physics texts (Born & Wolf,
Saleh & Teich, Jackson) use $\exp[i(kz-\omega t)]$ and $N=n+i\kappa$. All code here follows the slide convention. Whenever you
consult another book, check the convention first: most "wrong sign" errors in Fresnel phases, evanescent fields and
Kramers–Kronig relations come from mixing the two.
:::

## Using the code

All functions live in a small, readable module, [`optolib.py`](optolib.py), which you can import from your own notebooks:

```python
import optolib as ol
ol.fresnel(1.0, 1.5, 0.3)          # r⊥, r∥, t⊥, t∥ at 0.3 rad
ol.tmm([1, 1.38, 1.52], [100e-9], 550e-9)   # reflectance of a thin-film stack
```

See the appendix [Running the notebooks](running.qmd) for installation.
